zh: 在其历史的大部分时间里，共产主义的俄国在外部世界眼中，用温斯顿·丘吉尔那句著名的话来说，是“一个谜，包裹在神秘之中，又藏在谜团里面”。后来，一位美国驻莫斯科大使缓和了这一论断，给出了这样的判断：“苏俄不是一个谜；它只是一个秘密。”随着1989—1991年的崩溃，列宁和斯大林所建立的世界甚至连秘密也不再是了。七十四年乌托邦实验的详尽记录，如今已成为人人可读的公开之书。
en: For much of its history Communist Russia was perceived by the outside world to be, in Winston Churchill’s famous characterization, a “riddle, wrapped in a mystery, inside an enigma.” This verdict was later moderated by an American ambassador to Moscow to yield the judgment that “Soviet Russia is not a mystery; it is only a secret.” With the collapse of 1989-1991, the world that Lenin and Stalin built was no longer even a secret. The intimate record of seventy-four years of utopian experimentation is an open book for all to read.

zh: 苏联历史如今第一次真正成为历史，而这种终结使我们得以看清其生命历程的模式或“逻辑”。本研究力图勾勒这一模式，并探究驱动它的动力。
en: Soviet history is now for the first time really history, and this closure permits us to see the pattern or “logic” of its life course. The present study is an effort to delineate this pattern and to probe the dynamic driving it.

zh: 因此，下文首先是对苏维埃主义七十四年演变——从起源到终结——的综述性叙述。但更重要的是，本研究是一篇对苏联现象进行分析与阐释的长篇论文。因为我们从未直接感知那一现象，而只能透过一面昏暗的玻璃去观看。部分原因在于，直到几乎最后时刻，苏联现实始终是一个严密保守的秘密；部分原因则在于，其普世主义的社会主义抱负使它成为令世界其他地方不安的对象，有人受其吸引，有人则感到排斥。
en: What follows, therefore, is first of all a survey narrative of the evolution of Sovietism over seventy-four years as the system moved from its origins to its end. But even more, this study is an extended essay in analysis and interpretation of the Soviet phenomenon. For we did not perceive that phenomenon directly, but only as through a glass darkly. This was so in part because until almost the end Soviet reality was indeed a well-kept secret, and in part because its universalistic socialist pretensions made it an object of perturbing attraction or repulsion to the rest of the planet.

zh: 因此，西方观察者在谈论共产主义的俄国时，几乎总是在——哪怕只是间接地——谈论西方自身的问题与政治；这一情形使苏联研究成为社会科学中最富激情的领域。这种激情集中在这样一个问题上：苏联究竟是一种独特的“极权主义”，因而无法通过民主获得拯救，还是普遍“现代性”的一个变体，因而有能力达到真正的文明。而运用据称价值中立的社会科学范畴，也未能使解决这一问题变得更容易。因为使用这类范畴本身就构成一种价值判断，因为它们必然预设苏联体制是一种与其他社会机制并无不同的机制。
en: Thus, Western observers in talking about Communist Russia were almost always talking, if only indirectly, about Western problems and politics as well, a circumstance that made Soviet studies the most impassioned field of the social sciences. This passion focused on the issue of whether the Soviet Union was a unique “totalitarianism,” and therefore beyond democratic redemption, or instead was a variant of universal “modernity,” and therefore capable of true civilization. Nor did the application of the purportedly value-free categories of social science make the task of resolving this issue any easier. For the very use of such categories constituted a value judgment since they necessarily presupposed the Soviet system to be a social mechanism like any other.

zh: 因此，本书首先是一项努力，旨在厘清西方用以解读晚期苏联之谜的概念与范畴。从这个意义上说，它既是一部苏联悲剧的编年史，也是对二十世纪思想史相当一部分内容、对当代世界追求公正社会之努力的评论。然而，鉴于苏联社会主义在世界范围内的作用，对这场实验的历史解剖与这一意识形态评论无法彼此分离。但同样鉴于这场实验如今已是一个封闭的历史篇章，最终应当有可能比过去更为现实地进行这两项探究。本书的任务就是完成这一概念上的重估。
en: The present book, therefore, is above all an effort to come to terms with the concepts and categories with which the West has attempted to decode the late Soviet enigma. In this sense, it is not only a chronicle of the Soviet tragedy, but also a commentary on much of twentieth-century intellectual history and on the contemporary world’s quest for the just society. Given the worldwide role of Soviet socialism, however, the historical autopsy of the experiment and this ideological commentary cannot be disentangled. Yet, given also that the experiment is now a closed historical episode, it should at last be possible to conduct the two inquiries with greater realism than in the past. The task of this book is to effect this conceptual transvaluation.

zh: 本书使用的俄语术语转写系统为美国国会图书馆系统，仅作几处修改：在雅科夫列夫（Yakovlev）、叶利钦（Yeltsin）等如今已为人熟悉的名字开头使用“Ya”和“Ye”，在多斯托耶夫斯基（Dostoevsky）、托洛茨基（Trotsky）等较早为人熟悉的名字末尾使用“y”。软音符号省略。
en: The system of transliteration of Russian terms used here is that of the Library of Congress with a few modifications: “Ya” and “Ye” at the beginning of such now familiar names as Yakovlev and Yeltsin, and “y” at the end of such older familiar names as Dostoevsky or Trotsky. The soft sign is omitted.
